research_topic: Data Architecture Technology Stack for Tribunus: PGlite + Valkey + DuckDB + ElectricSQL + pgvector evaluation
transcript_summary: Deep research on the data architecture stack for Tribunus: PGlite (WASM Postgres), Valkey (Redis fork), DuckDB (OLAP), ElectricSQL (sync engine), pgvector, and PowerSync. The research evaluated each technology's capabilities, maturity, licensing, and architectural fit. ElectricSQL + PGlite form a tightly integrated Postgres ecosystem (server -> sync -> WASM Postgres in client). Valkey serves as coordination/streaming layer. DuckDB provides analytics. pgvector enables vector search in PGlite. PowerSync is a SQLite-based alternative with stronger mobile/offline story but source-available licensing.

research_findings.title: PGlite v0.4.6 - WASM Postgres for client-side database
research_findings.finding: PGlite is a full Postgres compiled to WASM (~3MB gzipped) running in browser (IndexedDB), Node.js, Bun, Deno. Supports pgvector, PostGIS extensions, live queries (live.query(), live.incrementalQuery(), live.changes()) for reactive subscriptions, and an alpha sync plugin (@electric-sql/pglite-sync) for syncing Electric shapes into PGlite tables. However, it is single-user/connection, no process forking, and the sync plugin is alpha with no outbound write sync or conflict resolution.

research_findings.title: Valkey v9.1 - Linux Foundation coordination/streaming layer
research_findings.finding: Valkey is the Linux Foundation fork of Redis (BSD 3-clause). API-compatible with Redis 7.2 for drop-in migration. Key capabilities: Streams with consumer groups (XADD/XREADGROUP/XACK/XCLAIM), sorted sets, pub/sub, TTL/expiry, hash field expiration (new in 9.0), search capabilities for AI workloads. Running on AWS ElastiCache since May 2026. Rapid development under Linux Foundation with Rust integration and cluster scaling improvements in progress.

research_findings.title: DuckDB v1.5.3 - Columnar analytics engine
research_findings.finding: DuckDB is an in-process OLAP columnar storage engine for analytical workloads. v1.5.3 (2026-05-20) with v2.0.0 expected Fall 2026 (breaking changes). Includes DuckDB-Wasm for browser-based analytical SQL. Supports SQL window functions, CTEs, complex joins, direct Parquet/CSV/JSON file querying read_parquet(), multi-threaded parallel execution, and a rich extension ecosystem (httpfs, parquet, json, excel, spatial).

research_findings.title: ElectricSQL 1.0 GA - Postgres sync engine
research_findings.finding: ElectricSQL is a Postgres read-path sync engine consuming Postgres logical replication (CDC) streams. Shapes provide partial replication with WHERE clauses and column subsets. Hub-and-spoke model: Postgres -> Electric sync service -> HTTP to any client. Client libraries for TypeScript, React (useShape), TanStack DB integration. Benchmarks show 1M+ concurrent readers, 99% CDN cache hit rate. Pivoted in April 2026 toward agent platform with Durable Streams and Electric Agents. Serverless agents announced June 2026.

research_findings.title: pgvector 0.8.2 - Vector search in Postgres/PGlite
research_findings.finding: pgvector 0.8.2 (2026-02-25) provides HNSW and IVFFlat indexes for approximate nearest neighbor search in Postgres. Supports multiple distance functions (L2, inner product, cosine, L1, Hamming, Jaccard), data types (vector float32, halfvec float16, bit binary, sparsevec), and binary quantization. Dimensions: vector up to 2000, halfvec up to 4000. Parallel index builds in 0.8.0+. pg_textsearch BM25 from ParadeDB complements pgvector for hybrid keyword+semantic search. pgvector runs in PGlite as a WASM extension.

research_findings.title: PowerSync vs ElectricSQL - sync engine comparison
research_findings.finding: PowerSync (Journey Mobile) offers SQLite-based bi-directional partial sync from Postgres, MongoDB, MySQL, SQL Server. Stronger mobile story with SDKs for Flutter, Swift, Kotlin Multiplatform, React Native. Production-ready write-back sync with JWT auth, upload queue, conflict resolution. SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA compliance (Jan 2026). TanStack ecosystem partner. Key limitation for Tribunus: uses SQLite not Postgres, so incompatible with PGlite/ElectricSQL's Postgres-native ecosystem. Licensing is mixed open-source/source-available (not fully Apache 2.0).

research_findings.title: PGlite sync plugin alpha - no outbound write sync
research_findings.finding: The PGlite sync plugin (@electric-sql/pglite-sync) is alpha stage. It supports inbound sync from Electric shapes into PGlite tables but has no outbound write sync (local PGlite writes do not propagate back to server) and no conflict resolution. This limits PGlite to read-replica scenarios currently. ElectricSQL's April 2026 pivot toward agent platform may shift sync engine development priorities.

research_findings.title: DuckDB v2.0 breaking changes expected Fall 2026
research_findings.finding: DuckDB v2.0.0 is expected in Fall 2026 with breaking changes. This means any integration code written against v1.5.x may need updates. The WASM variant will also need to be updated. Migration planning should account for this timeline.

research_findings.title: ElectricSQL pivot to agent platform may shift sync priorities
research_findings.finding: ElectricSQL (Electric) introduced Electric Agents and Durable Streams in April 2026, with serverless agents announced June 2026. While the sync engine (Shapes, CDC replication) remains core infrastructure, the company's product focus has broadened to agent orchestration. This may affect the pace of PGlite sync plugin development (outbound writes, conflict resolution).

implementation_specs.title: Tribunus Data Architecture - PGlite + Valkey + DuckDB Integration
implementation_specs.description: Implementation specification for the three-tier data architecture: PGlite (WASM Postgres) for local client-side database with pgvector and live queries, Valkey for coordination/streaming (streams, pub/sub, sorted sets), DuckDB for columnar analytics. ElectricSQL bridges server Postgres to client PGlite via shape-based sync.
acceptance_criteria: PGlite runs in browser with IndexedDB persistence, supports pgvector extension, and provides live queries
Valkey streams with consumer groups handle durable job queues between services
DuckDB-Wasm provides analytical queries on synced data in the browser
ElectricSQL syncs Postgres shapes into PGlite via the sync plugin
pgvector HNSW index enables semantic search on local PGlite data

implementation_patterns.code_example:
XADD task:queue * type analyze payload '{"id":"abc"}'
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 1 BLOCK 5000 STREAMS task:queue >
XACK task:queue workers entry-id

implementation_patterns.name: ElectricSQL shape sync into PGlite
implementation_patterns.description: Sync Electric shapes from Postgres into PGlite using the sync plugin's shape subscription API
implementation_patterns.code_example:
import { syncShapeToTable } from '@electric-sql/pglite-sync';
await syncShapeToTable(pg, { shape: { url: 'https://electric.example.com/v1/shape', params: { table: 'projects', where: 'owner_id = $1', bind: [userId] } }, table: 'projects_sync' });

implementation_patterns.name: Hybrid search with pgvector + BM25
implementation_patterns.description: Combine pgvector semantic search with BM25 keyword ranking for hybrid retrieval
implementation_patterns.code_example:
SELECT id, title, (1 - (embedding <=> '[0.1, 0.2, ...]')) * 0.7 + ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', title), plainto_tsquery('search terms')) * 0.3 AS score
FROM items
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 10;
